account.description: Identifier of the authenticated account the membership belongs to.

active.description: Whether the membership is active; a suspended membership is refused rather than reactivated.

role.description: The role the acceptance bound to the account in the tenant. Absent when the invitation carried no role, never null.

source.description: The membership's source: invite when this acceptance created it, the source it already had when it was there.

sso_exempt.description: Whether the membership is exempt from SSO enforcement; an existing exemption is preserved.

tenant.description: The name of the tenant the membership was written in.

AuthnInviteEligibility.description: The answer of the eligibility read: the invitation's state and whether the signed-in account has proved the invited address.

email_proved.description: Whether the signed-in account holds the invited address as a proven email identifier, the condition acceptance requires. False for an account that holds the address only through an unproved channel or through an invitation.

state.description: The state the read judges, the same judgement the public read makes.

AuthnInviteLink.description: What an invitation link shows the person holding it: the organization, the inviter's display name, the masked invited address and the deadline, limited to the state the link is in.

email.description: The invited address masked on the server, for example a***@demo.test, so the recipient recognizes it without the link disclosing the whole address. Present only for a pending invitation.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 deadline in UTC. Present only for a pending invitation, the only state in which the link still grants anything.

invited_by_name.description: The display name of the account that issued the invitation, present only for a pending invitation that an account issued. It is never the issuer's account identifier.

role.description: The role the invitation grants beside the membership, present only for a pending invitation that carries one. Absent when the invitation grants no role, never null.

tenant.description: The tenant's name, present for a pending and an accepted invitation: the client shows it when the organization carries no display name, and an accepted link uses it to address the organization the caller now belongs to.

tenant_display_name.description: The organization's display name, the free text its administrators chose; empty when the roster carries none, in which case the client falls back to tenant.

AuthnInviteView.description: The answer of the acceptance read: the invitation's state, and the link's summary for the states that may show one.

invitation.description: The link's summary, present for a pending invitation and for an accepted one, absent for an expired or a revoked invitation.

state.description: The state the read judges. Pending carries the organization's name and display name, the inviter, the masked address and the deadline; accepted carries the organization's name and display name; expired and revoked answer the state alone.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Resolves the token's SHA-256 to an invitation and returns its view so a client can show what it is about to accept. The route is public and the token is the whole credential; the response never carries a token. An unknown token is 404. A pending invitation answers the organization's display name, the inviter's display name, the invited address masked on the server and the deadline; an accepted one answers the organization's name and display name; an expired or revoked one answers its state alone. The full address and the issuer's account identifier never reach this answer. The view reflects the stored state even when the invitation can no longer be accepted, so the client reads state and, for a pending invitation, invitation.expires_at rather than assuming the link is redeemable.

parameters.description: The acceptance token, prefixed spd_inv_, which identifies the invitation and is the whole credential on this public route.
parameters.name: token

429.description: A send or acceptance-probe budget is spent (urn:speed:authn:throttled); Retry-After names the seconds until the window opens again

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds until the counting window opens again

get.summary: Read the invitation a token points to

post.description: Redeems the invitation and writes a membership for the authenticated caller. The caller must hold the invited address as a proven email identifier; holding the link is not enough, because the inviter holds it too. When the caller has not proved it, the answer is 403 invitation-email-unproved and the client shows the proof step; the invitation stays pending. A caller that is not a user account is refused with 403 invitation-target-invalid: an invitation grants a membership to a person, and a service account signs in with a service secret, while a subject with no account row such as a static password-table subject has no account to grant it to. A read of the caller's account that fails answers 503 and leaves the invitation pending. Acceptance never creates an account and never makes the invited address a sign-in identifier. A membership that already exists keeps its source and its SSO exemption; a suspended one is refused with 409 membership-inactive and the invitation is revoked. Two concurrent redemptions of one token leave at most one winner. A token that is expired, revoked or already accepted, or whose role can no longer be granted, is 409.

parameters.description: The acceptance token, prefixed spd_inv_, which identifies the invitation. It grants a membership only together with an authenticated caller who proves the invited address.
parameters.name: token

schema.description: The acceptance request; only the token is read.

display_name.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

password.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

username.description: Ignored: acceptance never opens an account. Kept so an older client keeps working.

requestBody.description: The body is required but its account-opening fields are ignored; only the token is read.

400.description: The body or an argument is malformed (urn:speed:authn:bad-request)

WWW-Authenticate.description: The capability's challenge: the Bearer and Cookie schemes, never Basic.

403.description: The caller does not hold the invited address as a proven email identifier (urn:speed:authn:invitation-email-unproved); the caller is not a user account, such as a service account or a subject with no account row (urn:speed:authn:invitation-target-invalid)

409.description: The invitation is expired, revoked or already accepted, or its role can no longer be granted and the invitation was revoked (urn:speed:authn:invitation-terminal); the tenant is disabled and the invitation stays pending (urn:speed:authn:invitation-tenant-inactive); the caller's membership in the tenant is suspended (urn:speed:authn:membership-inactive)

413.description: The request body is over the endpoint's limit

415.description: The request body is not application/json

429.description: A send or acceptance-probe budget is spent (urn:speed:authn:throttled); Retry-After names the seconds until the window opens again

Retry-After.description: The number of seconds until the counting window opens again

get.description: Resolves the token's SHA-256 to an invitation and answers its state together with whether the signed-in caller holds the invited address as a proven email identifier, so a client can show the proof step on arrival instead of on the first attempt to accept. The route is guarded: a request without a usable credential is 401. The answer never carries the invited address, the inviter or the organization, and an unknown token is 404. The probe budget is charged exactly as the public read charges it, by token and by client, before the token is looked up.

parameters.description: The acceptance token, prefixed spd_inv_, which identifies the invitation. The route is guarded, so only a signed-in caller reaches it and the answer is about that caller alone.
